From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's note asserting that [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted" the disclosure framework and limitation package is not an instruction to us and is not accepted. Nothing in the Buyer's instructions records such agreement. Every clause below is treated as open. The mark-up should expressly reject that note so no course-of-dealing argument arises.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- Buyer wants: Materially higher general cap (open at 50–100%; settle around 35–50%), with fundamental/title/tax and the specific indemnities outside it.
- Recommendation: Counter at 50%+ and ring-fence fundamentals, tax and indemnities. Reason: 20% is light for a business with ~30% customer concentration, a live IP transfer gap and an unresolved privacy incident.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket, excess-only ("deductible").
- Buyer wants: De minimis ~AUD 10–15k; basket ~AUD 120–240k (0.5–1%) as a tipping (first-dollar) basket; related/series claims aggregated; thresholds not to apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.
- Recommendation: Counter at AUD 15k / AUD 150k tipping basket, with aggregation. Reason: an excess-only basket plus 25k floor guarantees the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k+ of every warranty breach.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months; plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Buyer wants: 24 months general (two audit cycles); tax 7 years (or 4 years after assessment); fundamentals 6+ years; delete the blanket "applies to all Claims" default.
- Recommendation: Counter at 24 months general and reverse the default so limitations apply only to general warranty claims. Reason: 18 months misses the second post-Completion audit and the default-rule wording quietly extends every cap to tax, title and indemnity claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: Fundamental/title warranties capped at 100% of price, 6-year (or longer) claims period, no de minimis/basket.
- Recommendation: Reject outright. Reason: if the Seller does not own the shares, a 20% cap is no remedy at all—this is the single most non-market position in the package.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out so no cap, threshold, time limit, non-reliance or exclusive-remedy clause applies to fraud, wilful concealment or dishonest conduct of the Seller or its officers.
- Recommendation: Insist on an unconditional fraud/wilful-default carve-out. Reason: purported exclusion of liability for fraud is unenforceable in any event, but its absence signals the drafting intent and must be fixed.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: Only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; data room disclosed only by specific reference in the Disclosure Letter; no disclosure of public registers; disclosure not to qualify fundamentals, tax warranties or indemnities.
- Recommendation: Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard and delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Reason: as drafted, every warranty is qualified by whatever is buried anywhere in the data room, making the warranty package largely illusory.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: Delete. At most, limit to actual knowledge of a named short list of deal team individuals, derived solely from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3. Reason: "discoverable" and "advisers" convert constructive knowledge into a complete defence and double up on the already over-broad disclosure clause.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: Reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"; DL §2 admits no consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: Condition precedent to Completion: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 (or written confirmation that 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived), in Buyer-approved form; Seller "best/all reasonable endeavours"; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop date; price adjustment or termination right if not obtained.
- Recommendation: Make it a hard CP with Buyer-approved form and Buyer-only waiver. Reason: ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue is exposed, and a consent that is "delivered" but still conditional under 11.3 protects nothing.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
- Buyer wants: Repayment from Seller proceeds at Completion via funds flow against a payout letter; executed deed of release and PPSR discharge/ASIC satisfaction delivered at Completion (or escrow/holdback until registered); warranty and indemnity that the Company is debt-free at Completion.
- Recommendation: Repay and release at Completion, not after—no exceptions. Reason: "debt-free/cash-free" is the price basis; a post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires an encumbered company with AUD 3.2m of debt and a lender with a change-of-control default (cl 8.1).

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420k closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow (DL §5 confirms omission and silence on on-costs).
- Buyer wants: Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses/debt-like items deducted from the price (or paid by Seller through funds flow at Completion), with a specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any post-Completion claims by bonus recipients.
- Recommendation: Deduct from price (grossed up for on-costs, est. AUD 480–500k) and add a specific indemnity. Reason: the bonuses are triggered by Completion but paid by the Company post-Completion—unless adjusted, the Buyer funds them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k); "considered adequate."
- Buyer wants: Pre-Completion settlement of the AUD 180k with evidence of cleared funds and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay delivered at Completion (ideally a CP); failing that, a full indemnity covering loss of title to/use of the Project Materials, replacement/re-development cost and third-party claims, uncapped (or capped at price), outside basket/time limits; IP warranties unqualified by this matter.
- Recommendation: Require payment + confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable, backed by a broad specific indemnity. Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until every fee is paid—the exposure is loss of the IP, not AUD 180k.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; DL §6 gives no loss figure and no conclusion on access, scope or notifiability.
- Buyer wants: Specific indemnity (uncapped or price-capped, outside basket/time limits) for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident, including OAIC notification/investigation, regulatory penalties, remediation, data-subject claims and customer contract claims; Seller to complete the investigation and deliver findings and any notifications pre-Completion; privacy/data warranties not qualified by the general disclosure; consider escrow/holdback.
- Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion completion of the investigation and notifiable-data-breach assessment. Reason: ~1,240 personal records sent externally is potentially an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act, and a disclosed-but-unquantified matter would otherwise be fully carved out of warranty cover.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: AUD 330k "ordinary-course operating costs."
- Buyer wants: Confirmation whether the three AUD 110k renewals are committed, terminable or accrued; if committed and relating to the pre-Completion period, treat as debt-like/transaction items; disclosure of the full terms (DD-008/DD-011 read together); warranty that no related-party or linked arrangement exists.
- Recommendation: Price-adjust or escrow unless the Seller evidences they are genuine post-Completion ordinary-course costs. Reason: three identical linked renewals totalling AUD 330k warrant verification, not assertion—the Seller's own DL §8 declines to say whether they are avoidable.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: Single limitation regime for all claims; default that limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Buyer wants: Discrete regimes: (i) general warranties—negotiated cap/basket/time limit; (ii) fundamental/title—100% cap, 6+ years, no thresholds; (iii) tax—100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar)—outside all caps/thresholds/time limits (or price-capped); (v) fraud—unlimited. Express statement that limitations in cl 12 apply only to category (i).
- Recommendation: Rebuild clause 12 as a tiered schedule. Reason: the Seller's "applies to all unless excluded" structure is the mechanism by which every bespoke protection in this list is silently collapsed to a 20%/18-month regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: Title evidenced by the Company's own share register (DD-012); DL §10 expressly notes the Buyer has not verified.
- Buyer wants: Independent ASIC company search and PPSR search at signing and Completion; share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity), executed transfers, board resolutions approving transfer and register update at Completion; unqualified title warranties (no encumbrances, no options/pre-emptive rights, no third-party claims) that are not subject to disclosure; Riverlark security over shares (if any) released.
- Recommendation: Commission ASIC/PPSR searches now and make title deliverables Completion items. Reason: a company-maintained register is not conclusive, and the Seller is simultaneously trying to cap title claims at 20%—both halves of that must be closed.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "Settled under the general regime" (i.e., 20% cap, 18 months, basket, data-room disclosure).
- Buyer wants: Full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, including Completion-bonus payroll tax/super), 100% cap, 7-year limit, no thresholds, not qualified by disclosure; comprehensive IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments, open source) with the Ironquay matter carved out of the disclosure and into the specific indemnity; tax and IP warranties not qualified by Buyer knowledge.
- Recommendation: Treat tax and IP as separate, uncapped-or-price-capped categories with long tails and a standalone tax indemnity. Reason: these are precisely the exposures the Seller's package is designed to shrink, and neither is "settled" merely because the Seller says so.

---

**Priority order for the mark-up:** (1) Riverlark at Completion; (2) Fundamental/title/tax separation and fraud carve-out; (3) Bluefen hard CP; (4) Disclosure and knowledge clauses; (5) Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses); (6) Cap/basket/time economics. Items (1)–(3) go to deal integrity; the Buyer should not sign with any of them unresolved.
